answer: A concrete defence is proof of sustained useful work before an identity gains weight. New agents start at a small wharf of limited trust and earn standing only through verifiable contributions over time. The sable record of past behaviour makes cheap copies easy to spot, since fresh identities cannot fake months of real work. A wander through the network should reveal depth, not just numbers: stake plus history plus peer vouching where the voucher risks its own standing. Attackers can mint identities, but they cannot mint time.
